content:
Development of a Community Cohesion Strategy
2027 – 2032 with a two-year action plan 2026 - 28 and update
on wider community cohesion activity.
 

RESOLVED:
(a) That Cabinet notes the existing community
cohesion activity already being delivered across both councils
through the Community Hub and Be Together programme.
(b) That Cabinet approves the development of a
five-year community cohesion strategy that supports the Councils
motions for Fair treatment for all residents (South Oxfordshire
District Council, 23 October 2025), and Sanctuary and Fair
Treatment for All (Vale of White Horse District Council, 10
December 2025).
(c) That Cabinet notes the strategy will
finalise a fully funded action plan for the year 2027/28, linking
all existing grant funding and National Lottery funding into a
homogenous action plan. The strategy action plan will outline in
principle further actions that any future authority can consider
to support community cohesion.

Belong, a specialist third-sector organisation with recognised
expertise in developing cohesion strategies that link cultural,
social and economic factors to deliver best practice, to develop a
community cohesion strategy and action for the year 2027/28 for
Cabinet approval.

purpose:
To review and approve options for local plan
making.
content:
To review and approve options for local plan
making.


To RECOMMEND Council to:

(a) agree, subject to the agreement of South
Oxfordshire District Council, preparation of the next Joint Local
Plan for South Oxfordshire and Vale of White Horse
districts.

(b) agree the principle of governance to prepare
this new joint local plan under Section 15l of the Planning and
Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 and to delegate the detailed
arrangements to the Director of Legal and Democratic, in
consultation with the Director of Policy and Programmes and the
Cabinet Members for Policy and Programmes, and Legal and
Democratic.

(c) approve formal commencement of the South
Oxfordshire and Vale of White Horse Joint Local Plan 2045, in
accordance with the Town and Country Planning (Local Planning)
(England) Regulations 2026.

 

 

Subject to Council deciding to accept
recommendations (a), (b) and (c), Cabinet RESOLVED
to:

(d) approve the giving of a Notice of Intention to
commence local plan preparation (see Appendix 1), its publication
on the council’s website and making it available for
inspection.

(e) approve the Local Plan Timetable (as set out in
Table 1 of the report), its publication on the council’s
website and making it available for inspection.

(f) delegate authority to the Director of Policy and
Programmes, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Policy and
Programmes, to:

i. update and publish the Local Plan Timetable
monthly (or as required) to ensure an up-to-date timetable is
publicly available

ii. authorise commencement of a Scoping
Consultation

iii. undertake a self-assessment of readiness for
local plan preparation (at Gateway 1) and publish a summary
document

iv. approve, submit and publish documents to meet
Gateway 2 (Regulation 26) and Gateway 3 (Regulation 31)
requirements.

v. agree the content of and commencement of
consultation on proposed local plan content and evidence
(Regulation 23) and consultation on the proposed local plan
(Regulation 27).

(g) If (a) above is not supported, to agree the
preparation and production of a Vale of White Horse Local Plan and
to approve (d) – (f) above in respect of such a
plan.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to review and approve options for the preparation of the next Joint Local Plan for South Oxfordshire and Vale of White Horse districts.

content:
Cabinet member Councillor Hayleigh Gascoigne
introduced the report. The Project Officer was also online to
support questions. The policy explains the responsibilities of the
council in the statutory obligation to take ownership of
maintaining closed churchyards when transferred from parochial
parish councils. The new policy will ensure expectations are set
and helps the council to plan maintenance and ensure cost and
resource efficiency. There were long-term budget implications which
would be monitored. The policy supports the council to manage risks
whilst carrying out these duties to maintain public
safety.

A member asked about paragraph 13, on the special
expense levy. A member asked what the process would be to do this
if we wanted to. The Head of Finance explained it would need to go
through Cabinet and Council. The costs of the obligation will be
monitored in the budget.

Members agreed to accepting this policy when it was
put to the vote.

RESOLVED to  

(a) Approve the new Closed Churchyard
Policy  

(b) Delegate authority to the Head of Development
& Corporate Landlord in consultation with the Head of Legal and
Democratic Services to make minor amendments to the policy as
required.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a new Closed Churchyard Policy, delegating authority for minor amendments.
